title: Practice Paper—AI-Driven Behavioral Nudges for Organizations: An Integrative System for Sustainable Resource Management
authors: Christopher Amaral; Ceren Kolsarici; Iina Ikonen; Nicole Robitaille
eligible_reason: No staggered binary treatment. Phase 1 (Table 2) compares energy contribution on 18 curtailment-call days, common calendar dates for all firms, with firm random intercepts (lmer); Phase 3 (Table 6) is a randomized field experiment (23 experimental vs 16 control firms, time-invariant Condition) estimated by lme with random intercepts, ARMA errors and controls. Random effects in place of FE are not eligible (5b) in any case.
design_notes: Phase 1: lmer(Contribution ~ CurtailCallDay_in_window*Generator + CurtailCallDay_out_window*Generator + (1|ID)), hourly firm data, call dates identical across firms. Phase 2: demand forecasting (ARIMA, regression, NN, GBM, LSTM; Table 3). Phase 3: lme(ConsumptionAVG ~ Condition*CurtailCallNumHour + AnnualConsumption + Industry + Generator + Zone, random = ~1|ID, corARMA) on 351 firm-call rows (39 firms). Robustness (Web Appendix 3): lmer with CurtailCallHour*Year, same design.
data_files_note: Data for all phases shipped; Docs/readme.txt makes no statement about disguising or simulation.
data_provenance_note: Shipped firm-level data; no statement of simulation or noise. Not verified against published estimates.
software_notes: R (lme4, nlme, forecast, keras); one SPSS syntax file for Web Appendix 4.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text and papers/ checked Nov 2); the OpenAlex abstract in data/frame/mksc.jsonl is a one-sentence summary. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
